ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $DM$ and $EN$ are the perpendicular bisectors of $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, with footpoints $M$ and $N$. They intersect $BC$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. If $\angle DAE=20^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle$DAE=$20^\circ$,\\
then $\angle$ADE+$\angle$DEA=$160^\circ$.\\
Since DM and EN are the perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC respectively,\\
then AD=BD, AE=EC,\\
then $\angle$B=$\angle$BAD, $\angle$C=$\angle$CAE,\\
Moreover, since $\angle$ADE, $\angle$DEA are the external angles of $\triangle$ABD and $\triangle$AEC respectively,\\
then $\angle$ADE=$\angle$B+$\angle$BAD=$2\angle$B, $\angle$DEA=$\angle$C+$\angle$CAE=$2\angle$C,\\
then $\angle$B+$\angle$C=$80^\circ$,\\
then $\angle$BAC=$180^\circ$−($\angle$B+$\angle$C)=$\boxed{100^\circ}$.

ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $DM$ and $EN$ are the perpendicular bisectors of $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, with footpoints $M$ and $N$. They intersect $BC$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. If $\angle DAE=20^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle DAE=20^\circ$, then $\angle ADE+\angle DEA=160^\circ$. Since $DM$ and $EN$ are the perpendicular bisectors of $AB$ and $AC$ respectively, then $AD=BD$ and $AE=EC$. Thus $\angle B=\angle BAD$ and $\angle C=\angle CAE$. Moreover, since $\angle ADE$ and $\angle DEA$ are the exterior angles of $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle AEC$ respectively, we have $\angle ADE=\angle B+\angle BAD=2\angle B$ and $\angle DEA=\angle C+\angle CAE=2\angle C$. Hence $\angle B+\angle C=80^\circ$, so $\angle BAC=180^\circ-(\angle B+\angle C)=\boxed{100^\circ}$.

The figure also draws DM intersecting AB at M, EN intersecting AC at N, and there are perpendicular marks, indicating that DM and EN are the perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC respectively. Now reason: Let ∠B=∠ABC, ∠C=∠ACB. Because D is on the perpendicular bisector of AB, AD=BD, triangle ABD is an isosceles triangle, therefore ∠BAD=∠ABD=∠B. Because E is on the perpendicular bisector of AC, AE=CE, triangle AEC is an isosceles triangle, therefore ∠CAE=∠ACE=∠C. In triangle ADE, it is known that ∠DAE=20°, so ∠ADE+∠DEA=180°-20°=160°. Since DB and DE are opposite rays on BC, ∠ADE is the exterior angle at D of triangle ABD, so ∠ADE=∠B+∠BAD=2∠B. Similarly, at E, ED and EC are opposite rays, ∠DEA is the exterior angle of triangle AEC, so ∠DEA=∠C+∠CAE=2∠C. Therefore 2∠B+2∠C=160°, that is, ∠B+∠C=80°. So ∠BAC=180°-(∠B+∠C)=180°-80°=100°.
